newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Blix says Iraq probably still hiding nuclear data.
newsitem.headline: Blix says Iraq probably still hiding nuclear data.

text.p: Iraq is still probably concealing significant documentation about its clandestine nuclear weapons program and may also be hiding material and equipment, the director-general of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Hans Blix, said on Thursday.

"While recognizing that a very extensive documentation of the Iraqi nuclear program has been assembled...can we be sure that nothing further is withheld? The answer is no," he told the Security Council during a closed-door briefing.

Blix, whose agency is responsible for ensuring Iraq's nuclear weapons programme has been dismantled, said modern technology allowed the easy and quick transfer of written records into magnetic, optic, photographic or electronic media, which did not require much space and could be easily hidden or quickly removed.

According to Blix's briefing paper, which later became available, when he told a senior Iraqi official in June that the IAEA believed the "well-organised Iraqi government still retained a full record of its past nuclear programme, he indignantly denied this."
"However, such denials do not carry any weight. We cannot and do not act on the basis of trust. We still think it is probable that significant documentation is concealed and withheld.
"Some material and equipment could also be hidden and components of equipment could be moved around escaping even very thorough and rigorous monitoring," he added.
